quiz_met7:1.q: A hepatocyte in the fed state is building both fatty acids and sterols from acetyl-CoA. Besides the carbon source, what do both routes require?
quiz_met7:1.r: The overview slide places ATP and NADPH between the two branches, and the review slide says lipids are synthesized from acetyl-CoA and require both ATP and NADPH (p. 846, p. 871).

quiz_met7:10.q: During an overnight fast, glucagon rises and activates PKA in hepatocytes. In what state is acetyl-CoA carboxylase found?
quiz_met7:10.r: Low blood glucose raises glucagon, PKA phosphorylates acetyl-CoA carboxylase, and the phosphorylated form is labelled inactive; insulin acts through a phosphatase to reactivate it.

quiz_met7:11.q: After a carbohydrate-rich meal, hepatocytes make fatty acids without oxidizing them at the same time. The product of acetyl-CoA carboxylase prevents this futile cycle by inhibiting which enzyme?
quiz_met7:11.r: Malonyl-CoA inhibits carnitine acyltransferase I, which blocks formation of fatty acyl-carnitine and entry of fatty acids into the mitochondrion for beta oxidation.

quiz_met7:12.q: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase adds one carbon to make the three-carbon donor used by fatty acid synthase. What happens to that added carbon in each round of synthesis?
quiz_met7:12.r: Net addition is two carbons per cycle and the third carbon is lost as CO2 (p. 854); the CO2 leaves at the condensation step (p. 853).

quiz_met7:13.q: A patient on long-term parenteral nutrition without lipid supplementation develops dry, scaly, leathery skin. Which fatty acid is abnormally synthesized and accumulates?
quiz_met7:13.r: Absence of linoleic acid leads to abnormal synthesis and accumulation of the triene Mead acid (20:3).

quiz_met7:14.q: A fasting patient's adipocytes re-esterify some released fatty acids even though glycolysis in the tissue is low. How do these cells obtain the glycerol 3-phosphate backbone?
quiz_met7:14.r: Adipose tissue lacks glycerol kinase, so glyceroneogenesis (pyruvate to oxaloacetate to phosphoenolpyruvate to dihydroxyacetone phosphate) provides glycerol 3-phosphate when glycolysis is low or absent.

quiz_met7:15.q: A patient under prolonged stress has high glucocorticoid levels. According to the lecture, what happens to PEPCK expression in adipose tissue and to flux through the triacylglycerol cycle?
quiz_met7:15.r: Glucocorticoids increase flux through the triacylglycerol cycle by decreasing expression of PEPCK in the adipose; flux rises under stress.

quiz_met7:16.q: A healthy adult greatly increases cholesterol intake. According to the lecture, how does the body respond?
quiz_met7:16.r: Only about 25% of cholesterol usually comes from the diet, and in a healthy individual who consumes more, the body just makes less.

quiz_met7:17.q: After thiolase and then HMG-CoA synthase have each acted once, how many acetyl-CoA molecules have been consumed in total?
quiz_met7:17.r: Thiolase joins two acetyl-CoA into acetoacetyl-CoA, and HMG-CoA synthase adds a third acetyl-CoA to form HMG-CoA.

quiz_met7:18.q: A patient with high LDL begins a statin. Which molecule is the direct product of the enzyme this drug inhibits?
quiz_met7:18.r: Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, which converts HMG-CoA to mevalonate.

quiz_met7:19.q: A drug blocks the fourth and final stage of cholesterol synthesis. Which intermediate accumulates immediately before the block?
quiz_met7:19.r: The four stages run acetate to mevalonate, mevalonate to activated isoprene, activated isoprene to squalene, and squalene to cholesterol.

quiz_met7:2.q: A cultured cell line cannot form HMG-CoA but otherwise handles acetyl-CoA normally. According to the lecture's overview, which product can it still synthesize?
quiz_met7:2.r: Palmitate is made from acetyl-CoA through malonyl-CoA, while cholesterol and its products (steroids, vitamin D, bile acids) come from the HMG-CoA branch.

quiz_met7:20.q: The most heavily regulated step of cholesterol synthesis is assayed in hepatocytes under five combinations of hormone exposure and intracellular sterol level. Which combination gives the highest rate?
quiz_met7:20.r: HMG-CoA reductase is stimulated by insulin and inhibited by glucagon and by intracellular cholesterol (p. 863, p. 871).

quiz_met7:21.q: Cultured cells are loaded with cholesterol, and HMG-CoA reductase activity falls. Which mechanism does the lecture give for this effect?
quiz_met7:21.r: High intracellular cholesterol inhibits synthesis because it stimulates proteolysis of HMG-CoA reductase.

quiz_met7:22.q: A hepatocyte accumulates excess intracellular cholesterol. According to the lecture, how do LDL uptake by receptor-mediated endocytosis and ACAT activity respond?
quiz_met7:22.r: Intracellular cholesterol inhibits receptor-mediated endocytosis of LDL-cholesterol and activates ACAT, which converts cholesterol to cholesteryl esters.

quiz_met7:23.q: An enzyme defect prevents use of the last intermediate shared by the cortisol, corticosterone, and testosterone branches. According to the lecture's pathway, which steroid accumulates?
quiz_met7:23.r: Cholesterol gives pregnenolone, then progesterone, and progesterone branches to cortisol, corticosterone and testosterone.

quiz_met7:24.q: A patient cannot make the steroid that regulates renal reabsorption of sodium, chloride, and bicarbonate. According to the lecture's pathway, which hormone is missing and what is its immediate precursor?
quiz_met7:24.r: Aldosterone (mineralocorticoid) regulates reabsorption of Na+, Cl- and HCO3- in the kidney and is drawn as the product of corticosterone.

quiz_met7:25.q: A cell makes activated isoprene normally but cannot make cholesterol. According to the lecture, synthesis of which product is lost?
quiz_met7:25.r: Vitamin D, bile acids and steroid hormones come from cholesterol, while vitamins A, E and K and ubiquinone branch directly from isopentenyl pyrophosphate (activated isoprene) (p. 865, p. 846).

quiz_met7:26.q: A patient starts a statin. Based on the lecture's pathway map, synthesis of which mitochondrial electron carrier would also be expected to fall?
quiz_met7:26.r: Ubiquinone is a quinone electron carrier made from isopentenyl pyrophosphate (p. 865), which lies downstream of HMG-CoA (p. 846), the substrate of the statin-inhibited HMG-CoA reductase (p. 863).

quiz_met7:27.q: A child lacks functional lipoprotein lipase. Based on the lecture's transport routes, which particles would be expected to build up in plasma?
quiz_met7:27.r: Lipoprotein lipase acts at the capillaries on chylomicrons (exogenous pathway) and VLDL (endogenous pathway) to deliver fatty acids to adipose tissue and muscle; remnants and IDL form only after it acts.

quiz_met7:28.q: A researcher labels cholesterol in extrahepatic cells and later finds it delivered to the liver for disposal. Which lipoprotein carried it there?
quiz_met7:28.r: HDL scavenge cholesterol from the tissues and transport it to the liver for disposal, while VLDL and LDL carry cholesterol from the liver to the tissues (p. 871, p. 868).

quiz_met7:29.q: A 7-month-old boy has poor weight gain, loose fatty stools, dry skin and eyes, and hyporeflexia. Assembly of chylomicrons, VLDL, and LDL is impaired. Which of the following is defective?
quiz_met7:29.r: Abetalipoproteinemia is a defect in microsomal triglyceride transfer protein (MTP), with defective chylomicron, VLDL and LDL assembly and low circulating cholesterol and triglyceride.

quiz_met7:3.q: A hepatocyte is incubated with labeled acetyl groups, and the label appears in newly made palmitate. In which compartment did fatty acid synthase build it?
quiz_met7:3.r: The compartment slide lists fatty acid synthesis in the cytosol; mitochondria hold oxidation and the endoplasmic reticulum holds elongation and desaturation.

quiz_met7:30.q: A child with fat malabsorption has easy bruising and prolonged clotting times. The deficient vitamin is needed for which modification of clotting factors?
quiz_met7:30.r: Vitamin K is required for post-translational modification of multiple clotting factors through gamma-carboxylation of glutamate; deficiency causes bleeding, easy bruising and prolonged clotting times.

quiz_met7:4.q: A toxin selectively destroys the endoplasmic reticulum of hepatocytes while sparing the cytosol and mitochondria. According to the lecture's compartment map, which process is lost?
quiz_met7:4.r: Phospholipid synthesis is listed under the endoplasmic reticulum; ketone body synthesis, fatty acid oxidation and acetyl-CoA production are mitochondrial, and the pentose phosphate pathway is cytosolic.

quiz_met7:5.q: A hepatocyte lengthens palmitate to stearate. According to the lecture's compartment map, where can this lengthening take place? ER means endoplasmic reticulum.
quiz_met7:5.r: Fatty acid elongation is listed under both the mitochondria and the endoplasmic reticulum, and not under the cytosol.

quiz_met7:6.q: A hepatocyte is converting glucose carbons into fatty acids. In what molecular form do the acetyl groups leave the mitochondrial matrix for the cytosol?
quiz_met7:6.r: Citrate synthase joins acetyl-CoA to oxaloacetate in the matrix, and the citrate transporter carries citrate to the cytosol.

quiz_met7:7.q: During transfer of acetyl groups to the cytosol, one step on the return route to the matrix also supplies NADPH for fatty acid synthesis. Which of the following catalyzes that step?
quiz_met7:7.r: Malic enzyme converts cytosolic malate to pyruvate and CO2 while reducing NADP+ to NADPH; the slide marks this step 'Generates NADPH!'.

quiz_met7:8.q: A bodybuilder who eats large amounts of raw egg whites develops hair loss and a scaly red rash around the eyes and mouth. Which enzyme of lipid synthesis directly loses its required cofactor?
quiz_met7:8.r: Biotin (B7) is essential for acetyl-CoA carboxylase (p. 850), and raw egg whites contain avidin, a listed cause of biotin deficiency (p. 851).

quiz_met7:9.q: An infant with biotinidase deficiency has hypotonia, developmental delay, and seizures. Besides the first step of fatty acid synthesis, which reaction of the acetyl-group shuttle needs the same vitamin?
quiz_met7:9.r: Biotin is essential for pyruvate carboxylase as well as acetyl-CoA carboxylase (p. 850), and pyruvate carboxylase converts pyruvate to oxaloacetate in the shuttle (p. 848).

brief:
Met 7 High-Yield Tables

Met 7: Lipid Biosynthesis (Jones). This was your lowest biochemistry quiz in September at 14/32. Page numbers are pages of the combined PDF, where the lecture runs pp. 841 to 871. Everything is from her slides unless labeled (outside the slides). The slides never spell out ATP, NADPH, NADH, CoA, ACP, PKA, FFA, VLDL, IDL, LDL or HDL, so those expansions are standard names (outside the slides).

Where you were weakest in September

Your logged miss: palmitate is synthesized in the cytosol.

1. Precursors and critical intermediates (LO 1)

Every lipid starts from acetyl-coenzyme A (acetyl-CoA), and its two flagged intermediates are malonyl-CoA and beta-hydroxy-beta-methylglutaryl-CoA (HMG-CoA) (p. 846).
